title: Home that builds, the agentic way: "build it" to a running agent, the data reachable, a fuller EDA
request: The owner tested Home and found it not working: understanding weak, "ok build model" built nothing, synthetic data could not be found, 100,000 rows too many, plots and EDA not enough; "when the user says build, do everything automatically, the agentic way: make a plan and build"; "the chat bot must be agentic".
spec: A one-step build from the chat, the button or the Home agent's tool, handing the project to the agent that plans and runs it; a refusal with the step that clears it; a turn never silent; simulated tables at most 10,000 rows; every table downloadable and browsable; every column in the EDA; the outcome by column on the training rows.
plan: Reproduce each complaint live on the scratch server.
Build one quick_build path used by the route, the button (through the chat) and the agent's tool.
Hand the project to the intern so the plan and the run are the agent's.
Check it live on the owner's own draft, then review and fix.

decisions.decision: The button sends "Let's build the solution" through the chat instead of calling its own route.
decisions.why: One path: the chat answers with the plan or with what is missing, whatever started it.

decisions.decision: The outcome by column is computed in the project's data stage, not on Home.
decisions.why: Only the engine's locked split knows which rows are training rows; on Home the holdout is not yet fixed.

decisions.decision: The build hands the project to the intern rather than running the stages as a job.
decisions.why: The owner asked for the agentic way: the agent writes its plan, checks each stage and reports.

change: dclab_rnd/draft/api.py, chat.py, work.py, agentic/pool.py, accounts/guard.py, intern/loop.py, studio/engine.py, twin/claude.py, twin/design.py, twin/evaluate.py (new), twin/__main__.py, prompts home_agent and ai_first_home, Home and audit pages, Makefile, tests.

findings.scenario: The person typed it; the agent redrew the workflow and said it had not trained a model.
findings.cause: The build words were read only by the script, and the button opened a five-step wizard.
findings.fix: quick_build: the audit's proposal accepted, blockers checked, the project built and handed to the agent; the chat shows the plan.

findings.defect: The synthetic table could not be found or opened.
findings.scenario: The table was ready but the page showed only counts and three charts.
findings.cause: No route served a draft's table.
findings.fix: CSV download and a page of rows for every table, behind write rights.

findings.scenario: The agent took the number from the person's example (out of 100,000 bills).
findings.cause: The simulation tool allowed up to 200,000.
findings.fix: At most 10,000 rows from the chat.

findings.scenario: Home drew one histogram, one top-values chart and missing values.
findings.cause: The page used a fraction of the analysis it had.
findings.fix: Every column with its chart and numbers, time trends, correlations; the outcome by category or band on the training rows in the data stage.

findings.defect: Three messages in a row got no reply.
findings.scenario: Live: the person wrote past the open question; the model re-asked it, a no-op, and the turn ended.
findings.cause: The turn stopped after ask_user even when nothing was asked.
findings.fix: A turn that said nothing asks the open question again; a question from the person gets the plan so far first.

findings.defect: The build was refused with no way forward.
findings.scenario: Live: the problem had three linked parts whose map needed confirming.
findings.cause: The refusal was said as text only.
findings.fix: The refusal comes with its rule and the step that clears it: Confirm the map and build.

findings.defect: The agent trained on 3,000 of 100,000 rows.
findings.scenario: Live: the chat build chose quick mode for a table over 20,000 rows.
findings.cause: Quick mode was the default for large tables.
findings.fix: A chat build trains on the whole table up to 50,000 rows.

findings.defect: Claude's lane refused every call of a measured role.
findings.scenario: Live: the problem analyst's call was refused before it was sent.
findings.cause: With thinking on, the estimate counted 8,000 tokens of room against the role's €0.05 cap.
findings.fix: Measured roles answer without thinking, as they were measured.

findings.defect: A design version was cut and unreadable.
findings.scenario: Live: the leakage checkpoint's design stopped at its limit.
findings.cause: The limit was 3,200 tokens for a design of about 6,000.

findings.defect: "Build it" worked only in the server's default workspace.
findings.scenario: A tester in their own workspace typed it and nothing was built.
findings.cause: The builder was set on the default services only.
findings.fix: Every workspace's services get it when opened.

findings.defect: Sentences about the problem triggered a build.
findings.scenario: "I want to build a model to predict churn" built a project and started spending.
findings.cause: The build words matched anywhere in a short message.
findings.fix: Only a whole message that is an order builds.

findings.defect: The build tool's guard accepted any reply starting with yes.
findings.scenario: "Yes, the refund is known only after delivery" let the model build.
findings.cause: The agreeing word was not tied to an offer to build.
findings.fix: A bare yes counts only right after DCLab offered to build.

findings.defect: DCLab's accepted defaults were recorded as the person's choices.
findings.scenario: The ledger counted every column of the audit's proposal as a person agreeing with the rule.
findings.cause: The build saved the solution through the person's path.
findings.fix: The save carries its actor; DCLab's choices are recorded as the agent's; the agent's task is DCLab's words, not the person's.

findings.defect: Read-only members could download a whole table.
findings.scenario: A viewer downloaded an uploaded table as CSV.
findings.cause: The new reads were not listed among the routes that need write rights.
findings.fix: Both routes need write rights, as the code export does.

findings.defect: Some failures of the build ended in silence or a misleading message.
findings.scenario: An error inside the build, or the job limit after the project was made.
findings.cause: Only HTTP refusals were caught, and the agent's start after the build was not.
findings.fix: Any error is said in the chat; a job limit keeps the project link and says how to go on.

findings.defect: The first twin measurement counted the rules' answers twice and mixed two kinds of Claude answer.
findings.scenario: TWN-001 reported 12 judged cases (Claude 7, rules 2) for six runs; the evaluation page, reading the same runs, judged 6.
findings.cause: The measurement pooled each run's own answers with every version of Claude's expert record, each beside the same system answer.
findings.fix: Each run's answers are measured once and the expert record apart; TWN-002 stores the corrected matrix and names the result it supersedes (Claude 5 of 6, rules 1 of 6).

findings.defect: The live test's records were kept only in a temporary folder.
findings.scenario: 72 MB of transcripts, thinking, designs, conversations and the build sat in the session scratchpad, which a reboot clears; the evaluation page did not see them.
findings.cause: The live test server was pointed at the scratchpad.
findings.fix: The whole workspace copied (checksums verified) to agent_runs/live_tests/2026-10-16_phase3/, the twin runs into agent_runs/twin/, and the live server now writes there.

findings.defect: Creating a project from the chat had no clear button.
findings.scenario: The owner asked for a button that does what typing "build the model" did; the only one was "Let's build the solution" in the composer.
findings.cause: The one-step build was reachable by words and a small composer button that read like a wizard.
findings.fix: A primary "Create project from chat" button in the conversation's header sends "Create a project from this chat" (an order the build reads), shows Creating… until DCLab answers and Open the project once built; the wizard stays as Review step by step instead.

measurements.name: live build on the owner's fraud draft
measurements.gate: none: a check that the path works
measurements.result: The map confirmed from the chat, the project built, Claude as DCLab's agent planned, set the solution (is_fraud, time split, identifiers out), ran the five stages and reported holdout PR-AUC 0.478 (95% 0.368 to 0.615) against 0.12 at random, on 3,000 rows in quick mode.
limits: One draft, synthetic data; quick mode.

outcome: Home builds and trains from one word, the agentic way, and the data and its analysis are reachable.
lessons: Test the product as the owner uses it, in the owner's words, before calling a path done.
A word that starts an expensive action must be read as a whole order, never as a keyword.
risks: The rules' ranked guess for the outcome put a weekday column first on a blind sample; the target is still the person's to name.
